prediction.raw: 1. You are the asshole in this scenario. As the person in charge, it was your responsibility to ensure your brother got the sleep he needed, especially since you knew he's sensitive to sleep deprivation. Allowing him to stay up late, even if it was just for a couple of hours, was not a good decision, especially when you knew it would affect his behavior and mood the next day. While it's understandable that you didn't want to deal with a tantrum, it's essential to prioritize your brother's needs and well-being over avoiding a potentially embarrassing or exhausting situation. As his older sibling, it's your role to set boundaries and make decisions that are in his best interest, even if they're not the most convenient or fun. Additionally, downplaying the importance of sleep for a 7-year-old is not accurate. Sleep is crucial for children's physical and emotional development, and consistent sleep schedules help regulate their bodies and minds. Two hours of missed sleep may not seem like a lot to you, but it can significantly impact a child's behavior, mood, and ability to function the next day. It's also important to consider that your brother is still young and may not fully understand the consequences of staying up late. As his older sibling, it's your responsibility to guide him and make decisions that will help him develop healthy habits and routines. In this situation, it would have been better to gently but firmly encourage your brother to go back to bed, even if it meant missing out on some time with your friend. Your mom's trust in you to take care of your brother was misplaced, and you should take responsibility for your actions and apologize for not prioritizing your brother's needs.
